provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Int family batch. Licensed, biggest residential ticket; copy leans on budget ranges, timelines and living through the remodel. No cabinet, fixture or financing brands. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Cabinet door styles, countertop slabs, tile, plumbing fixtures and lighting, what to bring to the selections meeting, and the selections deadline before demolition starts
pageStructurePlus.why: Remodel buyers stall on choices, not on the contract. Showing how selections work, and when they lock, keeps the start date real.

pageStructurePlus.contains: The temporary kitchen setup, dust walls and floor protection, water and power shutoffs, which bathroom stays usable, and what a normal remodel day looks like
pageStructurePlus.why: Families with kids or a single bathroom delay for months because they can't picture living through demolition. Answering that is what gets the date booked.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Moving the sink or toilet, opening a wall, load-bearing checks, venting a range hood outside, and how each layout change moves the budget and the permit
pageStructurePlus.why: The biggest budget swing in a kitchen or bath is moving plumbing and walls. Homeowners decide their range once they know which side of that line they're on.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Curbless walk-in showers, blocking for grab bars, comfort-height toilets, wider doorways, slip-resistant tile and a bench in the shower
pageStructurePlus.why: Adult children often book this remodel for a parent and search by the problem, a tub that's hard to step over, not by a style.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Rough-in plumbing and electrical inspections, who pulls the permit, what a change order looks like on paper, and how hidden rot or old wiring behind the walls is handled
pageStructurePlus.why: Fear of surprise costs is why people get three bids and sit on them. A plain page about change orders makes the remodeler the safe pick.

designDirections.name: Estimate Sheet
designDirections.bestFor: Small remodel crews who win bathroom jobs on a fast in-home estimate and a clear budget range
designDirections.headlineSample: Kitchen and bath remodels in {City}, with the budget up front
designDirections.whyItFits: Steel blue and a clean grotesque read like a written estimate. The page drives to the consultation form and the budget-range page, nothing else.

designDirections.name: Room by Room
designDirections.bestFor: Remodelers with a deep file of finished kitchens and baths to sort by room, size and budget band
designDirections.headlineSample: Kitchens and baths rebuilt around how you live in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Terracotta Kiln, fails the CTA contrast rule. Driftwood keeps the same warm old-style serif with a walnut accent that passes, and lets cabinet and tile colour lead.

designDirections.name: Design-Build Studio
designDirections.bestFor: Design-build firms selling whole-kitchen and primary-suite remodels with a paid design phase
designDirections.headlineSample: Design-build kitchens and primary baths for {City} homes
designDirections.whyItFits: A private-bank cream and brass with a refined serif suits a project the family saves for over years, where they are hiring a designer as much as a crew.

openers.line: Your Google listing has a phone number but no website, so someone saving up for a kitchen remodel in {City} can't see a single finished kitchen of yours before they call.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what a kitchen and bath buyer would land on: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing opens your Facebook page. A couple planning a bathroom remodel wants to see finished baths by size and a budget range, not scroll a feed.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest kitchen or bath they shared there.
openers.linkLine: Your remodels sorted by room instead of by date: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site still shows a free-host banner and an old copyright year. Someone about to hand over a remodel deposit wants to know the kitchen company will be around for the punch list.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for a builder banner, an old copyright year or a dead contact form. Note which one you found.
openers.linkLine: The same remodeling company, current and fast: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your site on my phone and the kitchen gallery stacked into one long blur with the call button off screen. Remodel buyers browse on the couch at night, phone in hand.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note exactly what breaks: menu, gallery or call button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your kitchen and bath work, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Every couple thinking about a bathroom remodel searches what it costs in {City} before they call anyone. Right now they find other remodelers' numbers, not yours.
openers.hook: Search their site and social pages for any price or budget wording. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A budget-range page for kitchens and baths, in your words: {demo-link}

openers.line: The white-oak kitchen and the walk-in shower on your Instagram are strong remodel work, and they're buried under job-site reels. A gallery sorted by room would sell the next one.
openers.hook: Pick two finished rooms on their grid you could name by finish or layout. Mention one by name if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your kitchens and baths, sorted by room: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews talk about a remodel that finished on the week you promised and a crew that kept the dust off the hallway. None of that reaches anyone comparing kitchen bids.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about timeline, cleanliness or communication. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to the kitchens they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Late summer is when families start asking whether a kitchen remodel can be done before they host the holidays. The remodelers they find now get the autumn start dates.
openers.hook: Use this from July to early September. Name the holiday they'd be hosting in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready before the holiday kitchen rush: {demo-link}

openers.line: Remodel research happens after the kids are asleep. When a couple finally agrees on the bathroom at ten at night, there's no way to ask you for a consultation until morning.
openers.hook: Call their listed number after hours, or look for any form or booking link. If it's voicemail only, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A remodel consultation request that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a lead carpenter. Good remodel carpenters look at a company's finished kitchens before they apply, the same way homeowners do.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring story, a help-wanted note or a sign on the truck. Note the date of the post.
openers.linkLine: A remodeling site with a careers page for carpenters and tile setters: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your posts mention bathroom remodels in {City} and the towns around it, but there's no page telling someone in {Neighborhood} you work there. That town name is what they type.
openers.hook: Find the towns they mention in posts or reviews. Use the one with the oldest housing stock.
openers.linkLine: A kitchen and bath page for each town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you offer payment options on kitchen remodels, that belongs on the budget page. People decide whether to call based on whether a full kitchen can be split up.
openers.hook: Only if they mention financing somewhere: a post, a review, the truck. If they don't, skip this angle.
openers.linkLine: Remodel payment options explained before the consultation: {demo-link}

openers.line: A kitchen remodel means plumbing, wiring and permits. A page that shows your contractor licence and insurance answers the first question a careful homeowner asks.
openers.hook: Check the state contractor registry. Note that a record exists; never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence, insurance and permits on one remodel page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like a lot of your remodels come through designers and past clients. Even a referred couple looks you up before they let you into the kitchen, and a feed doesn't show the process.
openers.hook: Look for review text like 'our designer recommended' or 'friends used them'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a designer's remodel referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is a beautiful remodel. A kitchen or bath like that should be the first thing a stranger sees, not three scrolls down a feed.
openers.hook: Pick the newest finished kitchen or bath on their grid and name it exactly: room, finish and the neighbourhood if they tagged it.

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is lovely remodel work.

I was looking for kitchen and bath remodelers in {City} and found {Business Name} on social, but no site where someone can see your finished rooms or a budget range. I sketched a sample remodel site, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my last message got buried. Here's the sample kitchen and bath site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a gallery sorted by room, a budget-range page in plain words, and a week-by-week remodel timeline. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave you be.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for kitchen and bath remodelers here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss. Short version: I built a sample remodel site for {Business Name}, with kitchens and baths sorted by room, a budget-range page and a consultation form, plus marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email the link so you can look tonight?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many room and town pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a remodeler your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, which is a small slice of one bathroom."
"Can I walk you through it for fifteen minutes this week, Tuesday or Thursday evening?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and the budget page goes up first."

objections.objection: I get all my remodels from referrals and designers.
objections.handler: "Then your kitchens sell themselves. A referred couple still searches your name before letting you into the house, and a designer wants a link to send. The site is where both land."

objections.objection: I don't want to publish prices. Every remodel is different.
objections.handler: "Agreed, so we publish ranges by room and scope, not prices. Your words, your bands. It filters out the people who wanted a full kitchen for the cost of a faucet swap."

objections.objection: I'm booked out for months already.
objections.handler: "Good problem. The site lets you pick the bigger kitchens over the small bath jobs, and a waitlist form keeps those people from calling the next remodeler."

objections.objection: I pay for remodel leads from a lead platform.
objections.handler: "Those leads go to several remodelers at once and you pay whether you win the kitchen or not. Your own site sends that couple to one remodeler, you."

objections.objection: My partner handles the Facebook page and it works.
objections.handler: "Keep it. The Facebook page is great for regulars. The site is for the stranger comparing three kitchen bids, and every post can link back to it."
"{Build Range}. For you it'd be about {Build Price}, because it's a room gallery, a budget page, a timeline and a few town pages. That's less than the cabinet hardware on one kitchen."

email.subject: Kitchen and bath site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for kitchen and bath remodelers in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name}. I'll email you the link, have a look tonight. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} remodel demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, this is the stretch when families start planning a spring kitchen or bath and collecting bids. Thought of you.

The remodel site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a sliver of one bathroom remodel, never to an hourly rate. Remodelers think in projects and deposits.
The budget-range page is the core of the sale. Price it inside the build, but quote extra rooms or scopes as their own lines.
Price the gallery by finished project count, sorted by room, not by page count.
A consultation form that asks for room, rough size, budget band and start window is worth more than a contact form. Quote it separately.
Only quote design-phase or renderings pages for remodelers who actually sell a paid design phase.
Expect a slow close. Remodelers decide over weeks, so leave the demo up and follow up on their calendar, not yours.

lineItems.description: Max when the page has its own budget bands, a timeline, a gallery of finished rooms and an FAQ for that scope.

lineItems.item: Consultation form with room, size and budget band
lineItems.description: Max with photo upload, a start-window field, a designer-referral field and routing to two estimators.
Max with separate kitchen and bathroom timelines and a printable prep checklist for demolition week.
Max when the story covers the layout change, selections, budget band and a client quote.
Max when each town page gets its own finished kitchens and local permit notes.
Max with a checklist for adult children planning for a parent and a curbless shower gallery.
Max when the budget page, the timeline and the consultation form are all translated, not just the home page.

whatElseYouSell.name: Finished-room photo day with renderings
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One day at your three best finished kitchens and baths, styled and lit, plus two design renderings for the jobs you're bidding now."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or the week they finish a kitchen they're proud of.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile management for remodel projects
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every finished kitchen or bath goes on your Google profile with the town and the scope, so the map listing looks as busy as you are."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live and a remodel has wrapped.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests at the final walkthrough
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The day the punch list is signed, the homeowner gets a text asking for a review while they're still standing in the new kitchen."

whatElseYouSell.name: Instagram and Pinterest remodel content plan
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Remodel buyers start with saved boards of kitchens and showers. A steady plan puts your finished rooms on the boards they're building."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once there are enough finished rooms to post.

whatElseYouSell.name: Long-cycle remodel nurture emails
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A couple who asked about a kitchen in March might sign in October. A monthly note with a finished kitchen and a budget tip keeps you the remodeler they remember."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once the consultation form has collected a few names.

whatElseYouSell.name: Jobsite yard sign and dumpster banner artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The neighbours watch a remodel for weeks. A yard sign and a dumpster banner with your name and the site turn that into kitchen calls."

whatElseYouSell.name: January bathroom remodel planning push
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "People decide on the bathroom over the holidays when the family is over. A January push catches them the week they start getting bids."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in November, run in January.

whatElseYouSell.name: Open-house tour of a finished kitchen
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "With the client's blessing, one Saturday open house in a finished kitchen, with invitations to the street. Nothing sells a remodel like standing in one."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 4, when a client offers to show off their new kitchen.

withoutAI.route: The cabinet and countertop showroom they buy from
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your cabinet showroom sends homeowners to remodelers every week and its site is a catalogue. Introduce me and I'll build their find-a-remodeler page."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Showrooms have marketing budgets and want installed jobs, not browsers. Their remodeler list is a ready prospect list.

withoutAI.route: Independent interior designers who specify remodels
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The designer who sends you kitchens needs a portfolio site too, and your remodels are already in it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Designers buy websites on looks, and the remodeler's finished rooms are shared proof for both of them.

withoutAI.route: Licensed plumbers and electricians on their remodels
withoutAI.whoPays: The plumber or electrician, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Who does the rough-in on your kitchens and baths? I'll build their site, and your remodel page links to theirs."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Remodelers rely on the same few licensed subs on every job. One introduction from the general is a warm door.

withoutAI.route: Realtors pricing homes with dated kitchens
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Agents tell sellers the kitchen is holding the price back. They need a vendor page with a remodeler they trust on it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents recommend vendors for a living and pay for pages that make them look organised to sellers.

withoutAI.route: Home inspectors who flag bathroom leaks and rot
withoutAI.whoPays: The inspector, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Inspectors write up soft subfloors and failing shower pans every week. They need a site, and their buyers need a bathroom remodeler's number."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: A two-way referral: inspection findings become bath remodels, and the remodeler sends sellers to the inspector.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The appliance dealer whose ranges go into your kitchens sells to homeowners who still need a remodeler. A referral page benefits both of you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Dealers lose sales when the kitchen behind the appliance never gets built. A remodeler partner page fixes that.

withAI.route: Kitchen layout assistant for the cabinet showroom
withAI.pitchLine: "Shoppers sketch their kitchen walls and get a first cabinet layout to bring to the showroom, already sized to the room."
withAI.whyItWorks: It turns online browsers into showroom appointments with measurements in hand, which is what the showroom actually sells on.

withAI.pitchLine: "The designer drops a mood board in and gets a draft finish schedule for tile, cabinets and fixtures to edit, instead of typing it from scratch."
withAI.whyItWorks: Spec sheets eat a designer's evenings. A tool that drafts them is an easy monthly line.

withAI.pitchLine: "The plumber who roughs in your baths loses water-heater and repipe quotes to slow follow-up. Same follow-up tool you have, built for them."
withAI.whyItWorks: You already built it once, the second build is configuration, and the referral came from a client who trusts you.

withAI.pitchLine: "An agent uploads the listing walkthrough and gets a plain note on which kitchen and bath updates are worth doing before sale, with a remodeler to call."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents want a fast answer for sellers, and every note routes the work to one remodeler.

withAI.pitchLine: "Buyers get a plain summary of which bathroom and kitchen findings need a remodeler, not a forty-page report they never read."
withAI.whyItWorks: Inspectors compete on how readable the report is, and the summary sends repair work to the remodeler.

withAI.pitchLine: "The dealer's counter gets the same faucet, valve and shower-system questions every day. An assistant trained on their catalogue takes them."
withAI.whyItWorks: Dealers carry the support cost for every remodeler they sell to. Cutting repeat questions is an easy budget talk.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for remodel inquiries
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When you're on a demo day and miss a call, the caller gets a text asking which room, the rough size and when they hope to start."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their business number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Kitchen and bath budget estimator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner picks kitchen or bath, the size and finish level, and sees your budget band before they book. You stop driving to people who wanted a faucet swap."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their real budget bands by room, scope and finish level, and their minimum project.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts that name the remodel
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each new review gets a reply drafted in your voice that mentions the kitchen or bath, ready to approve from your phone."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside the review requests. Needs ten past replies to learn the voice. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Deposit and milestone billing for remodels
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Deposit at signing, then a draw at demo, rough-in, cabinets and final, each sent automatically when you mark the stage done."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their draw schedule and the payment account they already use.

softwareAI.name: Selections tracker with deadlines
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every tile, faucet, cabinet colour and slab choice in one list per kitchen, with the date it has to be locked before it holds up the job."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their standard selections list and the lead times they plan around.

softwareAI.name: Design rendering assistant from a room sketch
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Sketch the kitchen walls and pick finishes, and it drafts a rendering the couple can react to before the design meeting."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their common layouts and finish palettes, checked against finished jobs. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Remodel job board from consultation to punch list
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every kitchen and bath on one board: consultation, design, deposit, permit, demo, inspections and punch list, instead of a whiteboard in the shop."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once the form is producing. Needs their stages, who runs each one, and how they hand off to subs.

softwareAI.name: After-hours consultation line for remodel calls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers at night, asks which room, the size, the budget band and the start window, and books the in-home consultation."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once they trust you. Needs their calendar, scopes and the screening questions they always ask. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Client portal with daily remodel updates
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner sees today's progress, the next inspection and the selections still owed, and stops texting you at dinner to ask."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the job board in place first.

softwareAI.name: Change order drafter from site notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Find rot behind the vanity, talk into the phone, and it drafts the change order with scope, price and days added, ready for the client to sign."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their change order template and pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Permit and inspection reminder flow
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a remodel is booked, the permit filing, rough-in inspection and final inspection each get a reminder on the right day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their booking flow and which towns require which inspections.

softwareAI.name: Takeoff assistant for cabinets and tile
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the room dimensions and it drafts the cabinet run, tile square footage with waste, and trim for the supply order."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their layout rules and a few past material lists to check against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Sub schedule board for plumbers, electricians and tile setters
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each sub sees which kitchen they're in next week and gets a text when the job ahead of them slips."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, when they run two remodels at once. Needs their sub list and a typical job sequence.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on remodel budgets, timelines and permits
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'can we keep a working bathroom during the remodel' and 'when could you start' at midnight, from your real rules and schedule."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their FAQ, budget bands and current lead time, updated monthly. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Warranty and one-year walkthrough reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A year after the kitchen is done, the homeowner gets a walkthrough visit and a grout and caulk check. That's how the next bathroom gets booked."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a list of past remodels with completion dates.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by room and scope
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which remodels actually make money once cabinets, subs and change orders are counted: hall baths, primary suites or full kitchens."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs supplier invoices, sub bills and hours for a season of jobs.

softwareAI.name: Content writer for room and town pages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A new project story or town page each month, drafted from your job notes and finished kitchens, checked by you before it goes live."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their job notes and approval on every page. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Design-phase agreement and proposal builder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Turn the consultation into a paid design agreement in one click, with the scope, the rendering count and the fee credited to the remodel."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, only for remodelers who sell a design phase. Needs their design fee and a past agreement.

softwareAI.name: Supplier lead-time and price tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the cabinet shop's lead time moves or a tile price changes, the budget estimator and open remodel schedules update the same day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after the estimator. Needs their suppliers' price and lead-time sheet formats.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for carpenters and tile setters
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for remodel carpenter and helper jobs answer your usual questions, and you only call the ones with finish work to show and a valid licence where it's needed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves and the pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the remodel budget estimator for every remodeler
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built this kitchen and bath budget estimator for one remodeler. Every remodeler in the state is answering the same what-does-it-cost question by phone."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The hard part of vertical software is the workflow. The first remodel client taught it to you and paid for the build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Find-a-remodeler program for a cabinet manufacturer's dealers
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The cabinet manufacturer or regional distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your dealers' remodelers need a locator, spec sheets and a warranty sign-up. I've built that flow for a remodeler already."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers fund dealer marketing and have a channel problem. The remodeler client proves you know the trade.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The local remodelers' association, per bundle
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member remodeler a site template with a budget-range page and a timeline page as a benefit of joining."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need renewal reasons. One deal reaches dozens of remodel owners who already trust them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency builds remodel sites from scratch each time. License my kitchen and bath template with the budget page and room gallery built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell them the part you've already perfected.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Showroom network with installer pages for each partner remodeler
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The multi-location kitchen and bath showroom
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each showroom location gets a page per partner remodeler, so shoppers leave with a name and a booked consultation, not a brochure."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Showrooms only get paid when the kitchen gets built. A routed handoff is worth more to them than another catalogue page.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every bath remodel territory needs its own town pages and a consultation form routed to the right owner. I build it once and roll it out."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes many locations, all on the same template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Aging-in-place remodel referral portal for senior-care agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The home-care agency or area senior services group
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Care managers see a parent struggling with a tub every week. A referral portal sends those bathroom conversions to vetted remodelers."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Care agencies want safe homes for clients and a vendor list they can stand behind. The bathroom work is steady.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Design-centre upgrade pages for home builders
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Buyers who skip the builder's kitchen upgrades regret it a year later. A post-closing upgrade page routes them to one remodeler."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Builders like extra revenue and happy buyers. The remodel client becomes the builder's default kitchen partner.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Property-flipper kitchen and bath scope sheets
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Flippers need a fast kitchen and bath scope with a budget band on every house they walk. Sell them the sheet your remodeler already uses."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Investors buy tools that speed up offers, and every scope sheet points the remodel work back to your client.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Remodel cost sheet for lenders and appraisers
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Renovation lenders and appraisal firms, annually
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A quarterly sheet on where kitchen and bath scopes are landing locally, built only from bids remodelers choose to share with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Renovation loans need believable scopes. Built from contributed bids, it never claims more than the bids show.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Remodeling stack in a second metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A new kitchen and bath client in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I take one kitchen and bath remodeler per metro, and {City} is spoken for. The next metro over is open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the template, the pitch and the finished-room proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The remodeler whose web person vanished
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Half-built remodeling sites with no budget page are common. I can finish yours on a kitchen and bath template that's already live."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded remodelers already decided to buy. They need someone who can show finished remodel sites fast.

upsellLadder.offer: Remodel site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The remodel site and the care plan sit on one contract, so a new kitchen in the gallery is a text to me, not your Sunday."

upsellLadder.offer: Review requests at the final walkthrough
upsellLadder.trigger: The first remodel signed off since launch.
upsellLadder.line: "That bathroom you just handed over should be your newest review. Let's ask at every final walkthrough."

upsellLadder.trigger: They finish a kitchen they're proud of, or the room gallery still has fewer than a dozen projects.
upsellLadder.line: "Let's shoot your three best kitchens and baths properly. The gallery and a year of posts come out of one day."

upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of consultation-form data shows budget bands that don't match the scope asked for.
upsellLadder.line: "Half your remodel inquiries expect a different number. The estimator sets that before you drive out."

upsellLadder.trigger: The form has a list of couples who asked and haven't booked.
upsellLadder.line: "Those kitchen inquiries from spring are still deciding. A monthly note keeps you the remodeler they call."

upsellLadder.trigger: A remodel start slips because a tile or slab choice wasn't made in time.
upsellLadder.line: "That delayed kitchen start was a late selection. The tracker gets every choice locked on time."

upsellLadder.offer: Remodel job board from consultation to punch list
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention running two remodels at once or hiring a project manager.
upsellLadder.line: "Two kitchens and a bath at once won't fit on a whiteboard. Let's put every remodel on one board."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first anniversary of the earliest remodels since launch.
upsellLadder.line: "Last year's kitchens are due a walkthrough. Every one is a chance to book the bathroom next."
